title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Everyone
tiers.description: All employees, contractors, family and their Associates. Bound by the whole policy except paragraphs 1.4 (Associates procedure), 4.1 (margin lending/security), 4.2 (short-term/speculative/short selling) and 4.3 (hedging), and 5.3 (post-trade notification), which apply only to Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: (a) directors, officers and other KMP of any Latitude Group member; (b) any participant in the long-term incentive plan; (c) employees likely to come into contact with material price-sensitive information; and (d) any other person designated by the Company Secretary. The whole policy applies, including the margin lending/security, short-term/short-selling, hedging and post-trade notification provisions.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: A Designated Person; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Chairman of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Other Directors (including the Managing Director and CEO and Alternate Directors)
tiers.description: Designated Persons; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Chairman of the Board.

tiers.name: All Employees
tiers.description: The default clearance category for every discloser who is not the Chairman or another director: non-director Designated Persons and ordinary employees alike obtain clearance from the General Counsel or Company Secretary; only the Designated Persons within this group carry the post-trade notification obligation.

tiers.name: Associates of Designated Persons
tiers.description: Family members, trusts, companies, nominees and other persons over whom a Designated Person has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence. Subject to the whole policy, but prior notification, confirmation and post-trade notification (5.1-5.3) are handled via the Designated Person 'as appropriate to the circumstances'.

rules.detail: Company Securities is defined to include derivatives and other Financial Products, so dealing in a derivative is a 'deal' requiring prior notification and confirmation like any other dealing; the hedging/short-term bans in Part 4 do not apply to this tier.

rules.detail: Under the 'No hedging' clause, Designated Persons must not deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities except for dealing types permitted under this policy (i.e. ordinary share dealing under Part 5 and Schedule 2), so an OTC derivative such as a put or call is banned regardless of vesting.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law and under this policy.

rules.detail: Ban on transactions limiting exposure to risk on remuneration that has not vested; example given is a put option on incentive remuneration.

rules.detail: Same ban extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: has vested in the person but remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: A separate, unqualified limb bans dealing in any financial product over Company Securities 'at any time', with no vesting carve-out, except for dealing types otherwise permitted under the policy.
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law and under this policy.

exemption_authority: The General Counsel or Company Secretary may approve a Designated Person providing vested, unrestricted Company Securities as security under a non-margin-lending funding arrangement (clause 4.1). Separately, the Notification Officer may grant exceptional-circumstances confirmation under Schedule 3 to deal during a Prohibited Period or to dispose of securities despite a Part 4 restriction (e.g. severe financial hardship or a court order); a tax liability alone does not qualify, and 'other exceptional circumstances' are for the Chairman (or CEO if the Chairman is conflicted) to determine.

bespoke_clauses.topic: near-total hedging ban for Designated Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law and under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This unqualified limb of the 'No hedging' clause appears to ban an OTC put/call collar for Designated Persons regardless of whether the underlying shares are vested, unless it can be characterised as a dealing type otherwise permitted under the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Everyone - including all employees, contractors, family and their Associates | The whole Trading Policy with the exception of paragraphs 1.4, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3 and 5.3
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Employees who are not Designated Persons face no margin-lending, short-term or hedging restriction at all, but the directors and executives targeted for a funded collar will almost always be Designated Persons, so this carve-out is unlikely to be available to the client base.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing gateway for vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: The restrictions above do not prohibit other funding arrangements under which Company Securities may be included as security, however if a Designated Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement the prior approval of the General Counsel or Company Secretary must be obtained prior to agreeing to provide Company Securities as security under any arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the key gateway: a bank loan secured on vested, unrestricted Company Securities is expressly contemplated, subject only to prior GC/Company Secretary approval, separate from and additional to the ordinary Part 5 dealing clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you may request, and the Notification Officer may give, confirmation for you to ... dispose of Company Securities even if otherwise prohibited under Part 4.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Gives a discretionary route to force an unwind sale despite the margin-lending/hedging prohibitions in Part 4, for example on severe financial hardship or court order, though a tax liability alone does not qualify and the outcome is at the Notification Officer's discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A confirmation confirms that the proposed dealing is within the terms of the Trading Policy but does not otherwise constitute approval or endorsement by the Company or the Notification Officer for the proposed dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot treat a policy confirmation as validating the commercial terms of the collar or loan; the executive remains personally responsible for compliance with the insider trading law.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable for a Designated Person only over vested, unrestricted shares, and only through the section 4.1 secured-financing gateway rather than the general hedging clause. The 'No hedging' clause (4.3(b)) bans dealing in any financial product over Company Securities 'at any time' subject only to dealing types permitted under the policy, which on its face catches an OTC put and call regardless of vesting, so the derivative legs need to be structured as, or fall within, a permitted dealing type and clear the ordinary Part 5 notification and confirmation process (Notification Officer varies by role: Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman, Chairman of the Board for other directors and the CEO, General Counsel/Company Secretary otherwise), outside the closed periods, subject to a 5-business-day confirmation validity and the insider trading ban. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is expressly permitted for vested, unrestricted securities with prior approval of the General Counsel or Company Secretary, but is absolutely prohibited if the shares remain unvested or are still subject to escrow or a holding lock, and margin lending specifically is banned outright with no stated exception. Employees who are not 'Designated Persons' escape the hedging, margin-lending and short-term rules entirely, but this is unlikely to help the bank's target client base of directors and executives. Overall: the loan is structurally available for vested, unrestricted shares subject to GC/Company Secretary approval, but the collar's derivative legs face a real risk of falling foul of the blanket financial-product ban in 4.3(b) unless clearance can bring them within a permitted dealing type.
